clue.text: Climbed like a fish

blocks.note: first meaning: went up, as a ladder or a cliff
second meaning: covered in scales, as a fish's skin is

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a salmon leaping upstream; really the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of a verb for ascending and also an adjective for a body covered with scales.

clue.text: There could be a catch in it

definitions.text: There could be a catch in it

blocks.clueFragment: There could be a catch in it
blocks.note: surface reading: a suspicious offer with a hidden snag
setter's reading: a catch of fish, kept in an angler's wicker basket

explanation.walkthrough: A catch is usually a hidden drawback; here it is fish an angler has caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket an angler carries to hold the fish caught.

clue.text: Casanova's trophy?

blocks.note: surface reading: some prize a famous seducer might win
setter's reading: Casanova is the great lover, so his cup would be an amorous one; the real thing is a shared two-handled drinking vessel

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsy: a trophy is often a cup, and a famous lover's cup would be an affectionate one.
explanation.definitionFit: A loving cup is a large two-handled cup passed round at banquets, and also a trophy cup of that shape.

clue.text: Fraud takes a month to draw up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December
a tie is a drawn game

explanation.surface: A scam needs a month to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw up' looks like drafting a document; 'draw' is a tied match and 'up' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit is the act of misleading people dishonestly, which is what fraud amounts to.

clue.text: 24's sound, pure wool

indicators.note: the sound of another entry's answer means a word pronounced the same but spelt differently

blocks.note: the answer to 24 down is a hidden store, said the same as money
mere means pure or sheer, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: A label boasting that some fabric is made of nothing but wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is the fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, so the fabric name stands for a kind of wool.

clue.text: Rooks do have unpleasant repercussions

blocks.note: first meaning: what rooks literally do each evening, returning to their nests
second meaning: an idiom for bad deeds rebounding on the doer

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom about chickens (or rooks) returning to the nest is taken literally for the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says misdeeds eventually return to harm the person who did them, as birds return to nest at night.

clue.text: Delivered lines with vitality and beat

blocks.note: sent means delivered
RY is short for railway, the lines
go means energy or vitality

explanation.surface: An actor spoke his lines with energy and rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' and 'beat' suggest acting and music; a beat is a guard's patrol route.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentry-go is a sentry's duty of pacing to and fro on guard, which is a patrol or beat.

clue.text: Score 101, and total up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, the wrong way round

blocks.note: a sum is a total
101 in Roman numerals is C (100) plus I (1)

explanation.surface: A tally of points: 101, then add it all up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'total' look like arithmetic; the score is a written piece of music. Both pieces are reversed, in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written form of a composition, so it stands for music on paper.

clue.text: Party not to be confused with 12

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up out of their normal order

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 12 across

explanation.surface: A party that mustn't be mistaken for another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a warning to tell two things apart; really 'not' and the answer to 12 are the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is a formal social gathering, such as after a wedding, so it is a kind of party.

clue.text: Padre?

blocks.note: surface reading: a priest, so we expect a church word
setter's reading: a padre is a forces chaplain, a man in the armed forces who also leads church services

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the answer works both as a member of the forces and as a man who holds services.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain attached to the army, navy or air force, so he is a member of the military.

clue.text: Container for wine

blocks.note: first meaning: a large bag
second meaning: an old name for a dry white wine such as sherry, as drunk by Falstaff

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a wine box or bottle, but 'for' just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a big bag for holding goods, and sack was also the Elizabethan word for fortified Spanish white wine.

clue.text: Flatter, and rather dull?

blocks.note: bland means dull or insipid
the suffix -ish means somewhat or rather

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a flat, rather dull thing could be described another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like 'more flat', which matches dull; it is in fact the verb meaning to praise insincerely. The two wordplay pieces come in reverse clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax someone with flattering words or cajolery, an old verb for sweet talk.

clue.text: Pierce the wrong way - here's the right way to do it

definitions.text: here's the right way to do it

indicators.note: putting something the wrong way means arranging it out of its proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to pierce something properly after doing it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set of instructions showing the correct method for preparing a dish or achieving a result.

clue.text: Group of people in bar, talking

indicators.note: talking means we hear the word spoken rather than see it written

blocks.note: to block is to bar the way

explanation.surface: A group chatting together in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the verb meaning obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries, parties or people acting together for a shared purpose.

clue.text: Cleaning woman in the French neglige

blocks.note: la is the French feminine word for the
a negligee is a flimsy garment, and being in undress means being lightly or partly clothed

explanation.surface: A charwoman going about in a French nightgown.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose job is washing and ironing clothes and linen, a cleaning worker.

clue.text: Pine, in the early morning, turns to a different tree

indicators.note: in means one word is put inside another
turns means the letters so far are flipped round to read the other way
to means an extra piece is added on to the end

blocks.note: one in the morning, 1 a.m., with the Roman numeral I for one
to pine for something is to long for it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pine tree magically turns into another species before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree being defined, but it is the verb long. The early morning is 1 a.m., giving I and AM, and LONG goes between them before everything is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The magnolia is a flowering shrub or tree, a different species from the pine named in the surface.

clue.text: In addition to his need, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged in another way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something given on top of what a man actually requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In addition to' looks like a single phrase; the definition stops before 'to', which is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on the side is extra, carried out besides one's main work, so the phrase means additionally.

clue.text: Meal produced by Ruth, about right on cue'

indicators.note: about means one word goes round another

blocks.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth serves a meal right on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the most famous American baseball player of the 1920s; Ruth in the clue stands for his nickname Babe.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor meal of food grilled over charcoal, so it is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Replace suitor? Not I!

indicators.note: Not I tells us a letter I is to be left out

blocks.note: a suppliant is someone who humbly asks, a petitioner or suitor

explanation.surface: A lover is told he is being replaced by a rival, and protests that it won't be him.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of SUPPLIANT to get SUPPLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant someone is to take their place, often by scheming, so it means to replace or oust.

clue.text: The taste of seaweed

blocks.note: first meaning: a sharp distinctive flavour
second meaning: a dialect word for large coarse seaweed, kelp or wrack

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about the salty flavour of seaweed; 'of' only joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a strong sharp flavour, and tang is also a regional name for big brown seaweeds such as wrack.

clue.text: Highlight head of silvery hair

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of silvery
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Putting highlights in a head of silver-grey hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' and 'head of hair' suggest the hairdresser; the definition is the verb meaning emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, giving it prominence, which is what highlighting does.

clue.text: Fearlessly, for instance, braved ruin

indicators.note: something in ruin has been broken up and lies in a jumbled state

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fearlessly faced disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fearlessly' seems to describe how ruin was braved; it is actually an example of a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearlessly is a word ending in -ly that modifies a verb, the grammatical class of words that describe how something is done.

clue.text: Lose head in panic and make mistake

indicators.note: losing its head means the word has its first letter cut off

blocks.note: terror is extreme fear, panic

explanation.surface: Someone loses their head in a panic and slips up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make mistake' looks like the definition, but a noun is needed, so 'make' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a wrong action or a slip, so it is another word for a mistake.

clue.text: Make economies in connection with private home

blocks.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a private soldier's home at the front was the trench he lived in

explanation.surface: Cutting back on spending to do with a private house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private home' reads as a personal residence; here a private is the lowest-ranking soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back on spending, reducing costs in response to hard financial times.

clue.text: From America, cheques to deposit secretly

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: found running across the end of America and the start of cheques

explanation.surface: Sending American cheques to be banked on the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To cache something is to put it away in a hidden store, keeping it out of sight.

clue.text: Try to pay attention.

blocks.note: first meaning: to try a case in court, as a judge does
second meaning: to listen to and take in

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to make an effort to concentrate; 'Try' is really the legal sense of judging a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge is said to hear a case when trying it, and to hear is also to listen and take notice.

clue.text: Not, we hear, about to have romance and marry

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
romance is love
to get hitched is to marry

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to fall in love and get married.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Not' heard aloud as knot, the tying kind; the answer is one sort of knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a common sailing knot used to fasten a rope round a post, an example of a knot.

clue.text: Retinues can be grasping

indicators.note: can be says the letters could form something else if rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lord's entourage may be greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or greedy, describing someone eager to grab more.

clue.text: First in school we study a country

indicators.note: first in means only the opening letter of the word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of school
taken as written
a den is a private study or workroom

explanation.surface: A class's first lesson is about one nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a verb about lessons; it is the noun for a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation, so it is one example of a country.
